subject: Payment channel check-in — PO/card/marketplace decision needed
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Dawson <claire.dawson@atriahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-09T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + procurement channel options

Hi Claire — great call today, thanks for walking us through the integration needs. Short recap and asks so we have a clear path: 

What we covered:
- Target product: Redwood Hosted API for inference + Dedicated pool for compliance-bound workloads
- Expected Q3 pilot: ~100k tokens/day steady, burst to 300k/day
- Success criteria: sub-80ms median latency for gen routes, audit log export for 12 months

Options for payment/commercial path (you mentioned three possibilities):
1) Purchase Order (PO) via your AP process — standard for enterprise buyers
2) Corporate card — faster, but not always approved by healthcare procurement
3) Cloud Marketplace (Azure/GCP) — attractive if your marketplace purchasing is already in use

Immediate asks (can you confirm by EOD Tue?):
- Which payment channel is preferred for the pilot (PO / card / marketplace)?
- Any procurement forms / vendor questionnaire we should complete?
- Who is the primary procurement contact (email + phone)?

Attached is a lightweight procurement checklist and the draft SOW (SOW_v1). I'll follow up next week with a short mutual action plan once we have the channel confirmed.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Claire Dawson <claire.dawson@atriahealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@atriahealth.com>, procurement@atriahealth.com
Date: 2027-05-10T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement channel options

Thanks Ben — short update from procurement side: 

- Our preference is PO for anything tied to enterprise contracts, but we can use card if the pilot stays under $15k and legal signs off.
- Marketplace is attractive but requires that the offering be available under our Azure contract; we don't see Redwood listed there yet.
- I attached our vendor intake form (see: Vendor_Intake_Form.pdf — note: we only accept signed docs via DocuSign).

Blocked items right now:
- Legal needs a quick review of the SOW (approx 3–5 business days).
- Finance needs vendor onboarding (normally 7–10 business days once intake is complete).

I'll try to get procurement@atriahealth to confirm whether they can prioritize the vendor intake this week. Tom (cc) will own internal budget approval.

—Claire
Claire Dawson
Director, Clinical Integrations | Atria Health
claire.dawson@atriahealth.com | +1 (617) 555-1122
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Dawson <claire.dawson@atriahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, procurement@atriahealth.com
Date: 2027-05-11T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement channel options

Appreciate the note, Claire — helpful. Two quick clarifications: 

1) If you go PO, we can accept the PO and attach the signed SOW; lead time for onboarding is typically the same but gives you the enterprise controls you need.
2) For marketplace: we can pursue getting Redwood listed in your Azure contract, but that takes longer (4–6 weeks) — not ideal for a Q3 pilot start.

To unblock:
- Marissa, can your team pre-fill the vendor intake with the Redwood legal contact and send the DocuSign link for SOW_v1 so Claire's legal can start review immediately?
- Sean, can you confirm whether Redwood can temporarily accept card on an exception if procurement needs a faster route (we'll flag it in contract notes)?

Claire — if procurement can complete the intake this week and legal starts review, we should be able to scope a pilot kickoff in ~3 weeks. If intake stalls, I'll send a weekly nudge with a prioritization note for procurement.

Best,
Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-11T11:40:00-07:00

- Vendor intake: Marissa to upload vendor W-9, Redwood EIN, and engineer contact details.
- DocuSign SOW_v1: will be sent to Claire + Tom for signature; legal contact is legal@redwood.ai (Sarah Lim).
- Temporary card exception: Sean — please confirm whether Finance can approve a one-time card payment for the pilot (<= $15k cap).

Deliverables and ETA:
- Vendor intake uploaded: 2027-05-12 by 17:00 PDT
- DocuSign sent: 2027-05-12 by 12:00 PDT
- Formal reply from Atria procurement: TBD (Claire to confirm prioritization)

Marissa Cole
Strategic Accounts Ops | Redwood Inference

Subject: 1-week check-in: where is the procurement intake?

Claire / Procurement team — quick nudge on progress here as we prepare the pilot schedule next week. Current plan from our side:
- If intake + legal review are started by Friday 5/14, pilot kickoff remains targetable for the week of 6/7.
- If intake slips beyond 5/14, we'll need to push the kickoff and reallocate reserved capacity planning.

Can you confirm the current blocker (legal review / finance vendor setup / PO approval) so we know which internal owners to escalate to? If it helps, happy to have a 15-minute call today to unblock any questions.

Thanks — aiming to keep this moving without adding noise.

Ben
